column1: # card | field | proofs | source verdict | editorial verdict | independent source analysis | independent editorial analysis

middle-ages-great-famine|prompt-key|FA|PASS|PASS|Trokelowe explicitly says summer rains prevented grain ripening in 1315.|Medium: causal knowledge of this famine is thematic; frost/drought/locust/rain are parallel crop-loss causes. С чем accepts every С + instrumental answer, no weather-category error remains; key3 unique.

middle-ages-great-famine|note0|FR,FA|PASS|PASS|FAO reports April frost damaging winter cereals; Trokelowe gives summer rain as his cause.|Own useful fact about frost now present; attribution contrast is secondary, not a substitute for that fact. Clear Russian; no new claim about winter frost causing this famine.

middle-ages-great-famine|note1|DR|PASS|PASS|FAO defines drought as prolonged rainfall deficit with severe water scarcity.|Useful independent drought definition, fits засуха; short neutral Russian. Old famine-only binding cannot prove it, replaced here by actual FAO capture.

middle-ages-great-famine|note2|LC|PASS|PASS|FAO bioecology explicitly lists attacks on cereal crops and other plants.|Own useful crop-damage fact about locusts. Поедая растения и зерно is a reasonable general description of crop attacks, not a claim locusts caused the 1315 famine.

middle-ages-great-famine|note3|FA|PASS|PASS|Grain could not ripen and needed vessels for drying before bread making.|Useful description of wet harvested grain as well as cause; readable and tied to correct rain option. Can overlap explanation.

middle-ages-great-famine|explanation|FA|PASS|PASS|Whole Trokelowe excerpt confirms rain, drying, and lack of bread for the king at St Albans.|Two short coherent sentences explain cause and give a concrete consequence; no reference to an unproved modern diagnosis.

middle-ages-homage|prompt-key|HM,CB|PASS|FIX|1275 text explicitly associates joined hands and become your Man with homage; fealty on book is separate.|Easy assigned, but оммаж and коммендация are specialist ceremony labels, not broadly known adult facts. Four ceremony labels now parallel and grammatically clear; hands specify unique homage. Repair inside easy slot rather than reclassify.

middle-ages-homage|note0|FF,CB|FIX|PASS|Fief entry confirms concession of land/right/function; publisher summary lists investiture separately, but neither displayed passage defines investiture as transfer of fief or office.|Useful definition of the investiture alternative, concise; evidence needs a directly defining investiture passage, not a fief definition alone.

middle-ages-homage|note1|HM|PASS|PASS|1275 homage formula includes both hands and owe you Faith.|Own useful description of the ceremony and fealty pledge; standalone fact and not bare answer label. No novelty requirement beyond useful definition applied.

middle-ages-homage|note2|HM|PASS|PASS|Fealty section explicitly says Right Hand upon a book.|Concrete own fact about oath of fealty, relevant distinction with gesture of homage. Original vassal binding was inappropriate, actual homage/fealty text supports this.

middle-ages-homage|note3|CB|PASS|PASS|Publisher Summary explicitly discusses a separate model of commendation proposed by Le Gof and others.|Summary suffices for this limited literature claim; it is not a full chapter. Useful distinction, though wording научная литература is somewhat abstract; no fabricated complete-article claim.

middle-ages-homage|explanation|HM,CB,FF|FIX|PASS|Hands and declaration are directly supported; source distinguishes fealty, but 1275 text does not describe transfer of a fief as a third step.|Clear two-sentence account of homage; last clause needs a real investiture definition or narrower wording. Do not claim Fordham independently distinguishes a transfer ceremony.

middle-ages-tournament|prompt-key|TO|PASS|PASS|Tournoi entry defines several knights fighting singly or in groups, on horseback or foot.|Easy tournament concept is familiar; joust/melee/foot duel are credible same-domain alternatives, and two different combat forms select the umbrella tournament. Russian substitutions are complete noun labels, key3 unique.

middle-ages-tournament|note0|JO|PASS|PASS|Joute definition explicitly gives two mounted lancers trying to unseat each other.|Useful standalone joust definition, relevant to alternative. No need to explain wrongness beyond own fact.

middle-ages-tournament|note1|ME|PASS|PASS|Mêlée B1 defines confusion of combatants in hand-to-hand fighting.|Own useful definition of melee; not conflated with the organised event. Clear compact Russian.

middle-ages-tournament|note2|TO|FIX|PASS|Tournoi definition supports foot combat but does not establish exactly two fighters or a separate пеший поединок definition.|Literal is useful and plausible as a foot-duel definition; bind an actual duel definition rather than chevalerie institutional entry.

middle-ages-tournament|note3|TO|PASS|PASS|Entry includes different weapons and combat either mounted or on foot.|Adds useful пешком detail to prompt's mounted/group examples; overlapping the explanation is permitted. No bare-label note.

middle-ages-tournament|explanation|TO,JO,ME|PASS|PASS|Whole three lexical entries distinguish event and its combat forms.|Two sentences give concrete reason for key and resolve umbrella versus forms; smooth Russian, no obsolete code distractor remains.

middle-ages-joust|prompt-key|JO|PASS|FIX|Joute definition exactly gives mounted lancers and unseating opponent.|Easy assigned: rare Russian джостра is a terminology test not established as broadly known adult knowledge. Tournoi/меле/пешая дуэль now parallel combat concepts; пешая self-excludes from конный but remaining two do not make the rare term broad easy. Keep class/slot, repair fact.
middle-ages-joust|note0|TO|PASS|PASS|Tournoi supports combat mounted or on foot in multiple forms.|Useful fact about tournament breadth; fits alternative, clean Russian.
middle-ages-joust|note1|ME|PASS|PASS|Mêlée B1 supplies collective hand-to-hand combat.|Useful own definition; no claim it must only occur on foot or only at a tournament.

middle-ages-joust|note2|TO|FIX|PASS|Foot fighting at tournaments is supported, but one-on-one дуэль definition is not independently established by chevalerie or tournament alone.|Useful self-contained fact about foot duel, correct category. Needs proper primary lexical definition of duel.

middle-ages-joust|note3|JO|PASS|PASS|Joute A1 has two lancers charging toward each other and trying to unseat.|Useful complete definition of the term; overlap with tested fact accepted as useful explanation, not bare prompt/key string.

middle-ages-joust|explanation|JO,TO,ME|PASS|PASS|Three complete entries support lance duel, broader tournament and group melee.|Two concise sentences compare the forms; adequate explanation for general reader after reveal, though prompt still fails easy calibration.

middle-ages-excommunication|prompt-key|EX,ID|PASS|PASS|Excommunication excludes from communion, interdict does not cut off membership.|Medium distinctions between canonical measures are thematic; indulgence/interdict/penance all are church measures and plausible to unfamiliar players. Отлучение is a familiar word but distinction remains substantive, key2 unique, no grammar cue.

middle-ages-excommunication|note0|IN|PASS|PASS|Indulgence B1 explicitly remits temporal penalties for already pardoned sins.|Useful own theological definition; original heresy pointer was wrong and is not used. Neutral description, no assertion of purchase or absolution of guilt.

middle-ages-excommunication|note1|ID|PASS|PASS|Interdict definition explicitly distinguishes communion membership and territorial effect.|Own territorial restriction fact and relevant distinction. General local medieval context is clear; does not claim all possible interdicts must be territorial.

middle-ages-excommunication|note2|EX|PASS|PASS|Entry distinguishes full exclusion and sacrament restriction.|Useful definition of excommunication's effects, readable; permitted to explain correct term without inventing an extra anecdote.

middle-ages-excommunication|note3|PN|PASS|PASS|Penance article opening lists canonical punishment and a work of satisfaction enjoined on recipient.|Useful own fact about епитимья as imposed penitential act; source catholic context and Russian conventional term are coherent.

middle-ages-excommunication|explanation|EX,ID,PN,IN|PASS|PASS|All four actual definitions independently support the contrasts.|Two clear sentences explain person-level communion restriction against territory and penitential measures. No longer cites unrelated doctrine/tribunal definitions.

middle-ages-interdict|prompt-key|ID|PASS|PASS|General local interdict ordinarily affected medieval territories and almost completely suspended liturgical life.|Medium church-law concept, four coherent religious measures. Territory is distinctive and key2 unique. Generic запрещавшая обряды omits exceptions but does not explicitly say every rite without exception; acceptable short definition.
middle-ages-interdict|note0|IN|PASS|PASS|Temporal-penalty remission is defined in indulgence B1.|Useful standalone indulgence fact, clean Russian; does not substitute the heresy entry for proof.
middle-ages-interdict|note1|EX|PASS|PASS|Excommunication entry supports communion and sacrament restrictions on person.|Useful effect definition of the specific alternative, neutral and concise.

middle-ages-interdict|note2|ID|PASS|PASS|Article general local interdict has almost complete suspension of liturgy and sacraments; exceptions are listed.|Definition is useful and appropriately local; no claim of abolishing membership. More precise wording ограничивал would retain the documented exceptions, but current does not state absolute universal ban.

middle-ages-interdict|note3|PN|PASS|PASS|Penance opening confirms punishment or enjoined satisfaction.|Useful penitential-act definition, not tribunal claim. Can be shared with other card without making the tested main question a duplicate.

middle-ages-interdict|explanation|ID,EX,PN,IN|PASS|PASS|Original article differentiates local effect and membership; actual penitence/indulgence definitions cover last clause.|Two concise sentences give important population consequence, and contrasts. Reads as medieval general-local case rather than exhaustive modern taxonomy.

middle-ages-melee|prompt-key|ME|PASS|FIX|Mêlée B1 is confusion of fighters in hand-to-hand struggle.|Easy assigned, obscure Russian меле requires niche vocabulary, not broad adult knowledge. Four combat forms now parallel, and group-versus-single makes two self-exclude. Need an independently suitable easy fact in same slot, no automatic level change.

middle-ages-melee|note0|ME|PASS|PASS|Complete definition confirms mixed combatants and close fighting.|Useful standalone definition of correct term; overlap main fact is not alone a failure under clarification.
middle-ages-melee|note1|TO|PASS|PASS|Tournoi supports different weapons and individual or group contests.|Useful event breadth, own variant fact, clear Russian.
middle-ages-melee|note2|JO|PASS|PASS|Joute A1 explicitly specifies two lancers.|Useful joust definition; source sufficient, grammatically clean.

middle-ages-melee|note3|TO|FIX|PASS|Tournament text mentions foot fighting but does not define a solitary duel of two opponents.|Useful own definition, but author chevalerie pointer gives institution, not duel. Direct source remains needed.

middle-ages-melee|explanation|ME,TO,JO|FIX|FIX|Mêlée, tournoi, joute claims supported; пешая дуэль claim still lacks actual defining source.|Three sentences meet length contract, but source name and French spelling read as reference scaffolding rather than player-facing explanation. Explain the group-combat fact in Russian; bind duel fact correctly.

middle-ages-chivalry|prompt-key|CH,CO,VS|PASS|FIX|Chevalerie A supplies courage/loyalty/protection/courtesy as a wider institution/ideal.|Easy concept familiar, but only key is expanded Рыцарство как кодекс while others name component virtues; qualifier mirrors prompt ideal and signals umbrella answer. Align option granularity without padding wrong labels; key0/class unchanged.

middle-ages-chivalry|note0|CH|PASS|PASS|Entry explicitly lists courage and loyalty among knightly qualities.|Useful own ideal definition, honour reasonably summarized by moral ideal. No extra novelty requirement imposed.

middle-ages-chivalry|note1|CO|PASS|PASS|Courtoisie entry refers to medieval courtly ethics and refined courtesy.|Useful definition of courtly behaviour; bound tournoi did not support it, actual courtoisie does.

middle-ages-chivalry|note2|VS,HM|PASS|PASS|Vassal owes particular duties; fealty formula specifies lawful customs/services.|Useful relationship-specific fact about loyalty, distinct from general courage. No unsupported universal political allegiance claim.

middle-ages-chivalry|note3|CH|FIX|PASS|Chevalerie lists courage but does not define воинская доблесть as personal bravery and skill in battle.|Standalone useful virtue definition; direct definition of martial valour needed rather than mêlée combat definition.

middle-ages-chivalry|explanation|CH,CO,VS|PASS|PASS|Three complete entries support larger ethical ideal and its components.|Two readable explanatory sentences distinguish court etiquette and feudal obligations. Factually sound even while answer wording cues key.

middle-ages-pilgrimage|prompt-key|PL|PASS|PASS|Pèlerinage A1 defines religious journey to a holy place.|Easy broadly familiar practice; penance/veneration/indulgence are coherent religious alternatives, explicit journey selects key0. Correct Russian noun labels, no word-stem cue.

middle-ages-pilgrimage|note0|PL,GP|PASS|PASS|TLFi establishes journey, thesis introduction calls pilgrimage penitential and religious/spiritual; vow association is discussed in pilgrimage preparations.|Useful reasons for pilgrimage go beyond journey alone. Индивидуальное does not claim exclusively solitary travel. Overlap explanation accepted.
middle-ages-pilgrimage|note1|PN|PASS|PASS|Penance article defines sorrow and firm purpose of amendment.|Own useful fact about repentance, not about pilgrimage; concise player-facing Russian.

middle-ages-pilgrimage|note2|YK|PASS|PASS|York explicitly states physical proximity to body/relics for help and blessing.|Own useful devotional motive relates to Поклонение реликвии, not simply a generic journey. Helpful independent fact.

middle-ages-pilgrimage|note3|IN|PASS|PASS|Indulgence B1 specifies already pardoned sins and temporal punishment.|Own useful indulgence fact, directly sourced; no requirement to explain why wrong in this prompt.

middle-ages-pilgrimage|explanation|PL,GP,PN,YK,IN|PASS|PASS|Religious journey and penitential motivation supported; other practice definitions separately available.|Two short sentences distinguish travel from repentance/veneration/remission; readable and neutral. No unnecessary source/page jargon.

middle-ages-relic|prompt-key|RE|PASS|PASS|Relique A includes saintly bodily remains and associated objects.|Easy familiar religious object distinction; icon/container/crucifix credible similar sacred objects. Explicit remains separates key1, Russian complete and no absurd distractor.

middle-ages-relic|note0|IC|PASS|PASS|Icône1 defines panel painting with symbolic sacred value.|Own useful icon definition; does not claim every icon is on wood. Raw accented capture valid; unaccented failure excluded.

middle-ages-relic|note1|RE|PASS|PASS|Relique A directly defines remains or objects used by saint.|Useful standalone meaning of relic as a class of sacred object; not bare answer label. Clarified overlap rule permits this definition.

middle-ages-relic|note2|RQ|PASS|PASS|Reliquaire defines generally decorated variable-form container for relics.|Useful container function and decoration fact, relevant to distractor. No conflation container with contents.
middle-ages-relic|note3|CR|PASS|PASS|Crucifix definition explicitly includes cross bearing crucified Christ.|Useful own object definition; clean Russian and factual match.

middle-ages-relic|explanation|RE,IC,CR,RQ|PASS|PASS|Four complete lexical entries establish relic/image/container distinction.|Two clear sentences explain why remains/associated object is key; no misleading blanket claim crucifixes can never themselves become relics.

middle-ages-shrine|prompt-key|YK,MO,CA,EG|FIX|FIX|York supports saints/shrines as devotional loci, but does not define English shrine as a unique Russian Святилище among all listed sacred buildings.|Monastery/cathedral/church can all house and venerate relics; специально связано не excludes them. Shrine is devotional function, other options institutions/building types. Prompt lacks unique mutually exclusive key despite easy familiar domain.

middle-ages-shrine|note0|MO|PASS|PASS|Monastère A and B define religious community and common rule.|Own useful monastery definition, includes both monks and nuns. Does not present building as its only meaning.

middle-ages-shrine|note1|YK|PASS|PASS|York describes shrine miracle collections attracting pilgrims and veneration of saints.|Own useful devotional-place definition includes pilgrimage beyond storage; source supports practice, though Russian term needs clearer source at prompt level.

middle-ages-shrine|note2|CA|PASS|PASS|Cathédrale A explicitly says principal diocesan church and bishop seat.|Useful specific institutional definition; correct translated term кафедра and clear Russian.

middle-ages-shrine|note3|EG|FIX|PASS|Église II defines public-worship building but does not explicitly assert consecration in read definition.|Useful own church definition; narrow освящённое qualification needs a source or may be removed. No error HTML used as proof.

middle-ages-shrine|explanation|YK,MO,CA,EG|FIX|FIX|Definitions support functions but do not establish categorical opposition between shrine and those buildings; consecrated qualification in note not covered.|Two sentences are readable but imply competing exclusive classes although one church can contain shrine. Explain a distinctive supported fact after repairing unique prompt; no forced reclassification.

middle-ages-indulgence|prompt-key|IN|PASS|PASS|Indulgence B1 expressly remits temporal punishment for forgiven sins.|Easy well-known term plus precise misconception correction; four similar penitential concepts are plausible, all noun labels fit акт. Key2 unique, no false forgive-sin claim.
middle-ages-indulgence|note0|PN|PASS|PASS|Penance as virtue directly defines regret/hatred of sin and amendment.|Own useful repentance definition and effort to make reparation, clean Russian.

middle-ages-indulgence|note1|PN,IN|FIX|PASS|Read penance article submits sin to church jurisdiction but does not define confession as admission to a priest; indulgence anecdote has absolution, not that definition.|Useful ordinary definition of confession; author unrelated bindings not enough. Actual confession source required before factual certificate.

middle-ages-indulgence|note2|IN|PASS|PASS|Indulgence definition and examples describe prayer/pilgrimage bringing remission.|Useful conditions clause adds substance and avoids unconditional absolution. No obligation to invent a novel anecdote.

middle-ages-indulgence|note3|PN|PASS|PASS|Penance opening lists canonical punishment and work of satisfaction.|Useful own fact about епитимья, differentiated from remission. Russian terminology acceptable as penitential act.

middle-ages-indulgence|explanation|IN,PN|FIX|PASS|Temporal penalty and repentance/enjoined acts supported, but confession definition lacks direct source in supplied proofs.|Two concise useful sentences; only factual binding for confession remains to repair, not a new product decision.

middle-ages-market-town|prompt-key|GA|PASS|FIX|Introduction section4 explicitly calls urban status an important indication of trade and a market; same section also treats a mint as indicator.|Easy assigned: asks specialist gazetteer inference, not broad historical fact. Mint and market charter are also sensible evidence; which the gazetteer называет важным requires knowing its wording, not a unique general fact. Fix in easy slot; no technical padding.

middle-ages-market-town|note0|GA|PASS|PASS|Background ties fairs to feast days; section4 does not assume fair and market coexist.|Useful timing/limits fact about regular fair, coherent with alternative, not merely negating key.

middle-ages-market-town|note1|GA|PASS|PASS|Background states royal grants typically took charter form for rights to markets/fairs.|Own useful document fact. Makes this a credible indication of trade, reinforcing prompt ambiguity rather than proving it absent.

middle-ages-market-town|note2|GA|PASS|PASS|Urban status often only evidence of market, especially before1100.|Useful place-status definition/inference, not bare answer. Current note is general but supported, overlap explanation permitted.

middle-ages-market-town|note3|GA|PASS|PASS|Section4 expressly states mints were established at market centres and burhs.|Own useful coin-production indicator, not a fabricated distractor explanation. This valid alternative needs prompt differentiation.

middle-ages-market-town|explanation|GA|PASS|PASS|Section4 supplies urban-status inference; background and distinctions show markets/fairs cannot simply be equated.|Two clear explanatory statements if prompt is narrowly about methodology, but methodology itself remains unsuitable easy. Factual PASS doesn't certify card difficulty.

middle-ages-fair|prompt-key|GA|FIX|PASS|Background confirms annual fair, feast date and several days; read passage does not establish distant merchants in this wording.|Easy familiar fair versus weekly-market concept, same commercial domain. Periodic alone could include weekly market but feast and extended event distinguish key3. Source must cover distant-merchant qualification or omit it.
middle-ages-fair|note0|GA|PASS|PASS|Background says usually a market held once weekly on a set day.|Own useful scheduling fact about weekly market; no unsupported universality.

middle-ages-fair|note1|GA|PASS|PASS|First background paragraph says many markets at towns and also other settlements.|Own useful distribution fact relates to city market; not categorical city-only restriction.

middle-ages-fair|note2|GA|PASS|PASS|Background explicitly has fixed place so buyers/sellers know where to turn up.|Own useful coordination fact about market day, modest but informative and source-supported.

middle-ages-fair|note3|GA|PASS|PASS|Background gives feast day and variable duration, often several days.|Own useful duration detail beyond prompt; correctly scoped Английскую, no mandatory added novelty.

middle-ages-fair|explanation|GA|PASS|PASS|Full background defines annual feast-linked multi-day fair and weekly regular market.|Two clear sentences describe frequency and duration contrast. Doesn't assert every fair lasts multiple days.

middle-ages-toll|prompt-key|PE,GA,DU|PASS|FIX|Péage supports road/bridge/goods payment and gazetteer supports trading tolls.|Easy assigned but genus Пошлина includes Таможенная пошлина and market/Ярмарочный сбор under the question's broad за провоз или рынком wording. Three overlapping fiscal answers allow several readings. Need exclusive scope and parallel alternatives, key3 fixed.

middle-ages-toll|note0|DU|PASS|PASS|Douane A/B defines tax on import/export and border office.|Useful own customs-duty definition, clean Russian. Source proves it is a type of toll; cannot silently treat it categorically false.
middle-ages-toll|note1|GA|PASS|PASS|Monarch grants right to revenues including tolls from fairs.|Own useful fair-levy fact; explains charging domain without claiming exclusive economic category.

middle-ages-toll|note2|TX|PASS|PASS|Taxe C2 defines local levies for several services and local public income.|Own useful general local-tax fact; uses modern dictionary for generic concept, not proof of a particular medieval city policy.

middle-ages-toll|note3|PE,GA|PASS|PASS|Péage old use and medieval gazetteer jointly cover roads/bridges and markets.|Useful standalone meaning and examples, overlap tested fact accepted. Broadness still causes prompt/options defect.

middle-ages-toll|explanation|PE,GA,DU|PASS|FIX|Read sources support toll and specific customs/fair levies as narrower kinds.|Explanation admits types under the key, confirming options aren't exclusive. Source-correct contrast cannot resolve multiple possible answers to current broad prompt.

middle-ages-charter|prompt-key|CT,GA|PASS|PASS|Charte A defines authentic grant of rights/privileges; gazetteer says town charters confirmed rights/customs.|Easy familiar charter concept, four document types parallel. Records/protocol do not grant urban rights in these definitions, key3 unique; Russian grammar unambiguous.

middle-ages-charter|note0|RG,CT|PASS|PASS|Registre A1 enumerates facts/names/numbers; charter instead confers rights.|Own useful purpose of tax register, contrast secondary to accounting fact. Direct registre proof replaces old market passage.

middle-ages-charter|note1|RG|PASS|PASS|Entry A1 lists merchant/account/order registers and recording facts/names.|Own useful merchant accounting definition; no fictitious named medieval registry asserted.

middle-ages-charter|note2|PV|PASS|PASS|Procès-verbal A defines procedural act recording observations or depositions.|Own useful judicial record definition, relevant variant. No grant-of-rights confusion.

middle-ages-charter|note3|CT|PASS|PASS|Charte A authentic record of rights/privileges granted by lord.|Useful fuller charter definition, who grants privileges implicit. Overlap main fact is permissible as standalone meaning, not bare label.

middle-ages-charter|explanation|CT,RG,PV,GA|PASS|PASS|Actual definitions distinguish grants of town rights/customs from accounting/procedural records.|Two understandable sentences give reason for key and document contrast; no irrelevant market-source padding.

middle-ages-crusade|prompt-key|CS|PASS|FIX|Croisade A1 and Urban proclamation example support papally proclaimed expedition and cross-taking.|Medium assigned but принимали крест repeats the root of only Крестовый поход, giving key0 without thematic knowledge. Armed pilgrimage overlaps crusade context rather than mutually exclusive category. Remove cue and use truly parallel alternatives in same slot.

middle-ages-crusade|note0|CS|PASS|PASS|Definition and Urban example confirm cross and papal proclamation.|Useful definition with institutional context; accepted overlap with main fact. No invented need for unrelated anecdote.

middle-ages-crusade|note1|RC|PASS|PASS|Scanned chapter printed315 states final conquest of last Muslim possession in Spain in1492;319 specifies Granada.|Own useful endpoint fact about Reconquista, clear Russian. Scan is an11-page chapter extract, not whole monograph.

middle-ages-crusade|note2|JI|PASS|PASS|Review page119 introduction lists interiorisation of jihad as well as historical warfare.|Limited broader-than-war statement justified by announced interiorisation scope. It is a review first-page transcription, not Morabia's638-page thesis or complete119–125 review.

middle-ages-crusade|note3|GP|FIX|FIX|Thesis Approaches explicitly defines pilgrim for its purposes as unarmed; this passage cannot prove a fact about Вооружённое паломничество.|Note describes the opposite of its answer's defining adjective and is not an own useful fact of that variant. Retaining term with unarmed-person note does not close earlier source defect; replace within card scope.

middle-ages-crusade|explanation|CS|PASS|PASS|Definition/proclamation example support papal expedition and taking the cross.|Two sentences explain institutional authorization versus generic campaign. Source-correct explanation doesn't remove stem cue before reveal.

middle-ages-reconquista|prompt-key|RC|PASS|FIX|Chapter314–315 explicitly narrates expansion of Christian kingdoms into Muslim Iberia.|Same tested fact as history-spain-easy-01-04: naming the many-century Christian expansion against Muslim Iberia. Recording partner alone doesn't resolve. FIX reviewed card only with independent medium fact, keep ID/key1/class; partner read-only.

middle-ages-reconquista|note0|CS|PASS|PASS|Urban proclamation example has cross sign and expedition to Holy Land.|Own useful crusade institutional/sign fact; limited comparison to entire Iberian process is coherent. Does not assert Iberian campaigns never received crusade privileges.

middle-ages-reconquista|note1|RC|PASS|PASS|Scanned printed315/319 state1492 conquest of last Muslim Granada.|Useful endpoint addition beyond naming expansion. May occur in explanation and external partner note without independently duplicating main tested fact.

middle-ages-reconquista|note2|JI|PASS|PASS|Review introductory scope includes interiorisation beyond war narrative.|Own useful scope clarification for jihad; bounded source type and page119 transcription limitation retained.

middle-ages-reconquista|note3|GP|FIX|FIX|Thesis expressly defines its pilgrims as unarmed, not an armed-pilgrimage term.|Useful to ordinary pilgrims but belongs to a different answer than Вооружённое паломничество. No forced new definition invented; actual variant-specific source needed.

middle-ages-reconquista|explanation|RC|PASS|FIX|Printed314–315 supports Christian expansion and1492 completion.|Explanation repeats the same relation and endpoint as external partner; cannot solve duplicate by elaboration alone. Replace tested fact first, then rewrite explanation around it; no external edit authorized.

middle-ages-jihad|prompt-key|JI|PASS|FIX|First-page review describes combat in Allah's path joining community and religious duty of expeditions.|Medium assigned: на пути Аллаха makes all Christian Iberian/crusade/pilgrimage alternatives immediately untenable to an outsider. Need plausible Muslim-domain alternatives and meaningful thematic distinction; key1/class fixed. Source attribution is cumbersome but factual scope bounded.
middle-ages-jihad|note0|CS|PASS|PASS|Croisade A1/proclamation example supplies cross and papal expedition.|Own useful crusade fact; doesn't claim all Christian warfare qualifies.

middle-ages-jihad|note1|JI|PASS|PASS|Introductory review names interiorisation as one of thesis's four parts.|Useful caution against reducing jihad to war. Supported only as scope summary, not as full doctrinal treatment or universal current legal claim.

middle-ages-jihad|note2|RC|PASS|PASS|Scanned chapter says last Muslim possession conquered1492, identifies Granada.|Own useful Reconquista endpoint; clear concise note, no cue displayed before answer.

middle-ages-jihad|note3|GP|FIX|FIX|Unarmed pilgrim operational definition does not support armed pilgrimage alternative.|Mismatch with Вооружённое паломничество remains; source/own-variant failure, not mandatory explanation of why wrong.

middle-ages-jihad|explanation|JI|PASS|FIX|Review page119 supports religious-duty wartime account; current wording admits restricted coverage.|Second sentence about page119 рецензии is technical source-repair scaffolding, not useful player-facing explanation. Retain appropriate historical qualification in natural Russian; do not pretend complete review or thesis read.

middle-ages-pilgrimage-armed|prompt-key|GP|PASS|FIX|Introduction discusses Templars protecting pilgrims; Approaches defines unarmed pilgrims.|Medium assigned but asking whom protected while travelling to святыням is solved from broad pilgrimage definition; all four groups may travel, но паломников corresponds directly to religious journey. Query leaves protecting actor unnamed. Need substantive medium fact, not easy definition recast as research question.

middle-ages-pilgrimage-armed|note0|CS|PASS|PASS|Cross-taking and medieval Christian expedition defined in croisade A1.|Useful own crusader fact tied to group; concise and not generic expedition filler.

middle-ages-pilgrimage-armed|note1|GA,GP|FIX|PASS|Gazetteer proves trade events and thesis reviews travel infrastructure, but cited/read passage does not establish merchants' guarded trading routes.|Own useful merchant-role fact is plausible; need explicit commerce/transport/guard passage. Texas reconquista pages are not direct proof of this particular claim.

middle-ages-pilgrimage-armed|note2|GP|PASS|PASS|Approaches defines pilgrim as unarmed and unable to defend; intro specifies need for road protections.|Useful precise operational meaning and vulnerability beyond bare group label; limited to dissertation by current attribution.

middle-ages-pilgrimage-armed|note3|MO|PASS|PASS|Monastère A groups monks/moniales under common rule.|Useful own fact about monks via their shared-rule community. Now bound to actual monastery definition, not jihad review.

middle-ages-pilgrimage-armed|explanation|GP|PASS|FIX|Introduction discusses Templars defending pilgrims and Approaches unarmed definition.|First sentence useful; second disproves obsolete term вооружённое паломничество that isn't a current answer or question. Remove audit commentary, explain a substantive supported medieval fact instead. No runtime or ID rename.

middle-ages-black-death|prompt-key|BD|PASS|PASS|Boccaccio passage explicitly locates terrible plague in Florence1348.|Medium thematic date/location recognition, four historical calamities plausible enough to uninformed player.
